name: Bordeaux
blurb: Atlantic maritime climate on the Gironde estuary; Left Bank Cabernet blends and Right Bank Merlot dominate France’s most exported fine-wine region.

name: Burgundy
blurb: Continental Côte d’Or and surrounding AOCs; Pinot Noir and Chardonnay define village-to-grand-cru hierarchy from Chablis to Mâconnais.

name: Champagne
blurb: Cool northern latitude; sparkling wine from base wines of Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, and Chardonnay under Appellation Champagne rules.

name: Loire Valley
blurb: Long Atlantic-to-continental corridor; Muscadet, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, and Cabernet Franc shift by sub-region from Nantes to Sancerre.

name: Rhône Valley
blurb: Northern Syrah on granite slopes; southern Grenache blends under Mediterranean heat around Châteauneuf-du-Pape and the Côtes du Rhône.

name: Alsace
blurb: Rain-shadowed Rhine flank; aromatic whites (Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris) lead, with Pinot Noir as the main red.

name: Provence
blurb: Mediterranean coast and hinterland famed for pale dry rosés; Bandol Mourvèdre and coastal whites also feature.

name: Languedoc-Roussillon
blurb: France’s largest vineyard area; Mediterranean blends of Grenache, Syrah, and Carignan, plus Picpoul and Muscat near the coast.

name: Beaujolais
blurb: Granite hills south of Burgundy; Gamay is nearly exclusive for reds, with a little Chardonnay for Beaujolais Blanc.

name: Jura
blurb: Cool alpine-foothill AOCs; Savagnin (vin jaune), Poulsard, Trousseau, and Pinot Noir define a distinctive oxidative and sparkling tradition.

name: Savoie
blurb: Alpine valley vineyards; Jacquère and Altesse whites dominate, with Mondeuse as the signature red.

name: Southwest
blurb: Inland basins from Cahors to Madiran and Bergerac; Malbec (Côt), Tannat, and local whites such as Petit Manseng and Len de l’El.

name: Corsica
blurb: Mediterranean island with Nielluccio and Sciaccarello reds and Vermentino (Vermentinu) whites under AOC Corse and village appellations.
